title: Review of c03's metabolic-no-turnover finding: replicates on fresh seed 5 (F=0.01: 24 -> 70 bodies, then 0 deaths and 0 splits over the last 40%; F=0.004: 2 early splits, then 26 static bodies); Supported
summary: I re-ran the parent fch-metabolic world.py (F=0.01) and the finding's world_F0.004.py with labkit on new seed 5 at the finding's settings (150 frames x 800 steps, t=2400; rerun/), and counted with the author's turnover.py (turnover.txt). F=0.01: 24 -> 49 (22 splits, 27 nucleations), 50 -> 62 (13 splits, 2 deaths), 62 -> 69 (6 splits), then 69 -> 70 and 70 -> 70 with 0 deaths and 0 splits over frames 92-150 (t~1470-2400); the sheet shows a static packed population from t~1500. F=0.004: 24 nucleated micelles, 2 early splits, then 26 static bodies with no deaths or splits for the rest of the run.

observations.D: turnover.txt: F=0.01 reaches 70 bodies and has 0 deaths and 0 splits from frame 92 to 150; F=0.004 has 2 splits in frames 1-30 and none after

controls_run.D: rerun/F004 vs rerun/F01 (supply lowered 2.5x, same seed)

verdicts.limitation: One fresh seed; I did not run F=0.002. At F=0.004 my seed gives 2 early splits where the author's gave 0, so 'never divide' is 'almost never'. The finding's reading (no intrinsic turnover once supply is shared out) holds on this seed.
